safety_verdicts.content: Patient denies any chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations, headaches, or visual symptoms.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated captures denials of SOB, palpitations, headaches, and vision changes, but does not document denial of chest pain as stated in the gold fact.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to document denial of chest pain is primarily a ROS documentation gap; in this encounter it is unlikely to change immediate management of lower abdominal pain/urinary symptoms, but it could create ambiguity for future clinicians reviewing the note. The clinical risk is low because other cardiopulmonary negatives were documented and there were no chest-pain complaints driving the visit.

safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the specific 24–48 hour review window may delay reassessment if symptoms do not improve, which is important given possible alternative diagnoses (e.g., worsening UTI/pyelonephritis, appendicitis, gynecologic causes, pregnancy-related issues). Although general safety-netting was provided, a less urgent follow-up interval (“few days”) can increase the chance of delayed escalation and additional monitoring/treatment needs.
